title: Foundation by Act of Parliament
documented_change: The British Museum is established by Act of Parliament around the Sloane, Cotton, Harley and Royal library collections.
why_it_matters: Creates a national statutory institution and trustee structure.
what_remained: The institution did not yet operate under the modern NDPB/charity/accountability vocabulary.

title: Museum opens at Montagu House
documented_change: The Museum opens to visitors. The Museum’s own history notes that early access still depended on tickets and limited hours.
why_it_matters: Turns the statutory collection into a public-facing institution, but access was not yet equivalent to modern open admission.
what_remained: The statutory foundation remained; practical access arrangements evolved over time.

title: Access progressively widened
documented_change: Opening regulations and hours are progressively liberalised.
why_it_matters: The meaning of a 'public museum' changes in practice without requiring a wholly new institution.
what_remained: Core trusteeship and collection functions persist.

title: British Museum Act 1963
documented_change: The 1963 Act becomes the Museum’s principal modern statute and creates a separate body for the Natural History Museum.
why_it_matters: Recasts the modern trustee/statutory architecture; section 6 requires the Director to be appointed by Trustees with Prime Ministerial approval.
what_remained: Trustees remain responsible for safekeeping, care and public availability of the collection.

title: Exempt-charity framework
documented_change: Under the Charities Act 2011 the Museum is an exempt charity; DCMS is its Principal Regulator.
why_it_matters: Makes clear that charity-law duties coexist with public-body sponsorship rather than ordinary Charity Commission registration.
what_remained: Trustees remain the governing body rather than DCMS becoming the Museum’s board.

title: Cultural Freedoms status
documented_change: The Museum becomes part of the Cultural Freedoms regime, modifying specified operating and financial requirements.
why_it_matters: Adds operational freedoms without removing the Museum from central-government classification or sponsor-department accountability.
what_remained: Statutory duties and the public-finance relationship remain.

title: Governance Principles updated
documented_change: The Board’s Governance Principles state how trustees intend to discharge statutory, charity-law and public-body responsibilities.
why_it_matters: Makes the Museum’s internal governance rules more legible and explicitly incorporates Nolan/public-body standards.
what_remained: The British Museum Act remains the legal foundation; internal governance documents do not replace it.

title: Collection-security crisis disclosed
documented_change: On 16 August 2023 the Museum announces that collection items had been found stolen, missing or damaged and that police were investigating.
why_it_matters: Turns collection security, documentation, trustee oversight and internal controls into central governance questions.
what_remained: The Museum’s statutory duty to safeguard and care for the collection was not newly created by the crisis.

title: Nicholas Cullinan becomes Director
documented_change: Nicholas Cullinan takes office as Director in June 2024.
why_it_matters: Changes executive leadership during the post-2023 governance and recovery period.
what_remained: The Director remains responsible to Trustees; the statutory appointment architecture persists.

title: Security and governance remediation enters formal risk reporting
documented_change: The annual report identifies loss/theft and damage to the collection as risks and lists documentation/digitisation, new security procedures and a collection audit among mitigations.
why_it_matters: Shows the 2023 crisis becoming embedded in formal risk-management and organisational-control processes.
what_remained: The report is management’s own account of mitigation; effectiveness requires independent or subsequent evidence.

title: New DCMS framework agreement
documented_change: DCMS and the Museum publish a formal framework agreed under Managing Public Money and approved by HM Treasury.
why_it_matters: Spells out the present sponsor relationship: central-government classification, NDPB status, exempt-charity status, Principal Regulator, appointments, accountability and financial controls.
what_remained: The framework expressly says it creates no new legal powers; statutory authority remains rooted in legislation.

title: Framework updated
documented_change: The 2025–28 framework is updated, including clarification of support for the Treasure Valuation Committee through a Museum subsidiary.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates that the administrative architecture itself is a living document that can change between statutory reforms.
what_remained: The underlying British Museum Act and trustee duties remain.
